executiveSummary: GM0356 passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract and has a coherent 2025 administrative base: 66,788 residents, 39 neighbourhoods in 22 districts, one BAG place/settlement, no ProRail station, 78 scheduled-transit stop areas and eight logical A2/A27/N210/N408/N409 road links. Published neighbourhood rows sum to 66,780 residents, eight below the municipality control (-0.012%), and that rounding difference is retained. Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Nieuwegein is a dense urban Lek, Lekkanaal, Doorslag and Merwedekanaal junction with the Prinses Beatrixsluis, a drinking-water intake pathway, major motorway/tram corridors and a 24/7 emergency department. Its own climate vision says a Lek-dike breach can reach 1-6 m in low Fokkesteeg within hours, while HDSR reports both adjoining Lek trajectories assessed far below the current standard due principally to piping and requiring strengthening. The model instead emits an exact internal river inundation scalar of 1.316626 through T+72, 28,666 affected resident-equivalents and 1,982,760.112 deprived person-hours without selecting a Lek hydrograph, defence segment/state, breach, hydraulic grid, arrival or recession. Eight active T+24 presets reuse one neighbourhood ranking led by Binnenweides and Burgen, even though official flood evidence specifically identifies low Fokkesteeg and an unprotected but water-robust extramural area. Pluvial stress becomes exact zero at T+72 without the city's rain, terrain, sewer, groundwater or pump model; public water, hospital, antenna, education, electricity-capacity and Waterinfo layers remain context and do not prove incident state or physical continuity. First-72-hour evacuation, hospital continuity, A2/A27/tram/bridge/sluice access, water-intake protection, prolonged-outage support and verified recovery milestones are absent. Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static/planning values are never zero, dry, safe, open, operational or recovered.

identity.summary: Official 2025 code, name, province, safety region, boundary edition and centre containment agree.
notes: Feature id, municipality bundle and manifest all identify GM0356 Nieuwegein in Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht.
The generated centre 5.0964444, 52.0313003 lies inside the generalized 2025 CBS boundary.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent but inadequate for the Lek defence, canal, hydraulic, sewer and access mechanisms.
notes: The urban municipality meets Lek, Lekkanaal, Doorslag and Merwedekanaal systems and includes protected, extramural and water-robust areas.
Generalized polygons do not encode Lek-dike segments, piping/stability, protected side, canal/lock compartments, intake protection, hydraulic cells, terrain or road/tram/bridge intersections.
HDSR strengthening and the RWS intake programme are current/planned management context, not present operational state or completed protection.

demography.summary: Municipality totals and rounded neighbourhood rows reconcile within expected CBS publication semantics.
notes: Official municipality population is 66,788; published neighbourhood rows sum to 66,780, a -8 (-0.012%) difference.
Summed neighbourhood households are 31,305 and age-65-plus residents 14,445; the municipality age-65 share is 21.6%.
Rounded, suppressed and null cells remain source values or Unknown and are not rewritten to force equality or infer assistance/priority.

regionalDetail.summary: The 39-neighbourhood bundle is useful demographic context but has null fields and no physical hazard or service calibration.
notes: Population, age and doctor/supermarket distance are complete; home-value coverage is 31/39 and several housing/social fields cover 33 or 34 of 39.
District-heating and public-charging fields are null in all 39 neighbourhoods and remain NoData.
Water, hospital, antenna, education, capacity and Waterinfo features are map context with affectsSimulation=false and cannot establish network continuity or current state.

settlements.summary: The single BAG place and single woonkern label for Nieuwegein are internally coherent.
notes: The BAG place centre lies inside the generalized boundary and the BRT settlement layer contains one woonkern.
One settlement label does not erase operational differences among Vreeswijk, Jutphaas, Fokkesteeg, City, business parks, extramural areas and canal/lock sites.
Registered population is not incident-time occupancy at hospital, schools, tram stops, workplaces, shipping or events.

transport.summary: Road and scheduled-transit identity is plausible, but bridges, waterways, tram and event-valid destination access are incomplete.
notes: Eight logical links connect Utrecht, IJsselstein, Houten and Vijfheerenlanden via A2, A27, N210, N408 and N409; repeated A2/A27 edges are series connections, never additive capacity.
There is no ProRail station inside; 78 GTFS stop areas represent tram/bus schedules, not live operation or evacuation capacity.
The graph does not select bridge/lock/canal state, local feeder access, hospital approach, direction, closure, hazard intersection, accessible throughput or alternative route.

emergencyContext.summary: Regional/local flood, hospital, intake and 72-hour evidence is strong context but actionable capacities and state remain unverified.
notes: Official sources identify severe breach consequences, dike deficiencies, evacuation, source-water incident pathways and regional long-duration response pressure.
St. Antonius has a dated 24/7 SEH questionnaire record but no live occupancy, staff, diversion, generator, water, supply, access or restoration state.
The municipality asks residents to self-support for 72 hours, but no household compliance, neighbourhood support-point network, stocks, staffing or communication fallback is exposed.
Net congestion and statutory priority are planning context, not live outage or guaranteed hospital/water/rail restoration.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute at all six checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0356 pnpm audit:model gate passed both focused contract tests.
Inline Vite SSR reproduction captured every preset at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 plus a controlled local wildfire without creating a repository scratch file.
Earthquake is direct-zero at T+24/T+72, coastal has zero direct inundation but wind/service burden and canonical wildfire has smoke but no local flame; none is an all-clear statement.
Outputs are deterministic exercise indices and resident-equivalents, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties, operator states or commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal ledgers and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains within [0,1], values are finite/non-negative, no-event behavior is exact and repeated runs are deterministic.
Every service allocates all 39 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 66,788 residents; local demand/delivery closes and layer selection does not mutate the scenario.
Arithmetic correctness does not validate hydraulic state, physical lifeline topology, transient occupancy, action feasibility or recovery timing.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A source-free river scalar and common cross-hazard neighbourhood order contradict official flood and mechanism-specific evidence.
notes: River internal floodDepthM is 1.316626 from T+24 through T+72 without a named Lek event, defence segment/state, breach, connected grid, velocity, arrival or recession.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire all rank Binnenweides, Burgen, Hagen, Driften-Zuid, De Liesbosch, De Wiers, Graven en Gravinnen and Doorslag-Oost first in the same T+24 order.
Official breach evidence instead identifies low Fokkesteeg for rapid deep water and separately distinguishes an extramural but water-robust area; neither relation governs allocation.
A controlled municipality-centre wildfire produces flame 0.790576 and smoke 0.560146 while retaining the same generic ranking rather than eligible fuel/perimeter/exposed-object evidence.

serviceDependencies.summary: Lek/canal water control, intake protection, hospital continuity, multimodal access and utility dependencies are absent or synthetic.
notes: Road links support logical mobility/supply only, but lack local geometry, direction, bridge/lock/tram state, event passability, hospital and response destinations or real throughput.
The 146 HWH features, four current Waterinfo observations, Prinses Beatrixsluis and Lekkanaal intake do not form an approved dike-canal-pump-sewer-intake graph or influence recovery.
St. Antonius, Stedin territory/sample, 111 antennas and 68 education sites provide facility/context identity but no physical continuity, backup, priority, occupancy or restoration edges.
Exact service percentages remain synthetic indices and cannot be presented as operator availability.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but selected events, accountable actions and evidence-valid observations are outside the causal graph.
notes: Hazard/service contribution ledgers reconcile, but the four Waterinfo observations correctly remain affectsSimulation=false and no hydrograph/breach/defence state is selected.

A foreseeable breach needs pre-impact warning, evacuation versus vertical shelter, extramural-area instructions, hospital continuity/transfer, traffic management, water/lock actions, rescue and re-entry decisions.
A source-water incident needs substance/source, navigation/industrial incident state, intake decision, sampling/quality, alternate supply and public-health advice.
Actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification, uncertainty and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound disruption is directionally conservative, but exact plateaus and rapid clearance are not locally calibrated.
notes: River T+72 retains scalar 1.316626, severity 0.411985, 28,666 affected and 1,982,760.112 person-hours; service availability ranges from drainage 0.350631 to mobility 0.788483, with most values identical to T+24.
Compound T+72 retains scalar 0.457021, severity 0.511247, 37,126 affected and 2,371,611.275 person-hours; all services are exact T+24-to-T+72 plateaus except facilities declines further.
Pluvial direct stress and affected population become exact zero by T+72 and local-wildfire forcing becomes zero at T+48 without drainage/fire all-clear evidence.
Official municipal evidence explicitly says post-flood dry, passable, habitable and liveable timing is unknown; model recovery must retain this Unknown rather than infer milestones.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, regional assignment and rounded demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0356 is Nieuwegein in Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht. The centre is inside the boundary; 39 neighbourhood rows total 66,780 against 66,788 official residents (-8, -0.012%).
findings.action: Retain official controls, source edition, rounding/suppression and Unknown semantics; never force neighbourhood rows to equal the municipality total.

findings.summary: The model quantifies Lek inundation without selecting a river or defence event.
findings.evidence: The internal floodDepthM scalar is 1.316626 at T+24 and T+72, with 26,704/28,666 affected resident-equivalents and 499,698.517/1,982,760.112 deprived person-hours. No Lek hydrograph/datum, trajectory 15-1/44-1 state, piping/breach/overtopping case, protected side, cell grid, velocity, arrival, recession, issue time or probability is selected.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing depth, exposure and recovery until RWS/WMCN, HDSR and VRU select a versioned event. Retain the scalar only as a synthetic diagnostic; unselected cells remain Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: Rapid Fokkesteeg inundation, pre-breach evacuation and extramural-area decisions are absent.
findings.evidence: Nieuwegein states that low Fokkesteeg may reach 1-6 m within hours and evacuation occurs before breach; it separately identifies an unprotected but water-robust area. The model begins at impact and provides no warning lead, zone, evacuation-versus-vertical-shelter choice, dependent-person support, route/destination, hospital decision, rescue or verification.
findings.action: Add pre-impact through T+72 owner/trigger/action ledgers for warning, zone-based evacuation or shelter, extramural instructions, vulnerable-person assistance, hospital continuity/transfer, traffic control, rescue, aftercare and re-entry.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active presets reuse one neighbourhood order that conflicts with official flood geography.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Binnenweides, Burgen, Hagen, Driften-Zuid, De Liesbosch, De Wiers, Graven en Gravinnen and Doorslag-Oost first. Official evidence identifies Fokkesteeg as the low rapid-depth area; heat, cyber, fire/smoke, rain and river mechanisms require different physical surfaces or targets.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and source/target/exposed-object intersections; preserve unsupported cells as Unknown and use deterministic ties only after evidence-derived values.

findings.summary: Pluvial, groundwater, subsidence and heat outputs ignore the municipality's governing climate evidence.
findings.evidence: The municipality documents historic 50 mm/h rain, sewers not designed for peak/long rain, above-ground routing, up to 5 C current urban-rural felt-temperature difference, drought/groundwater/subsidence and vulnerable groups. The model gives pluvial scalar 0.413723 at T+24 then exact zero at T+72, and heat 23.543 C/severity 0.082593 without a hyetograph, terrain/sewer/groundwater state, shade/surface/building exposure or current observation.
findings.action: Integrate the governing climate-atlas/stress-test rasters and metadata, sewer-overland-groundwater model and heat exposure/vulnerability inputs; display scenario deltas separately from weather observations and preserve cell NoData.

findings.summary: The distinctive Lek-Lekkanaal-lock-pump-sewer-intake system is visible but non-causal.
findings.evidence: RWS identifies Lekkanaal drinking-water production and incident risks from shipping/nearby businesses; the map shows Beatrixsluis and 146 HWH structures plus four current Doorslag/Lekkanaal observations. None supplies an approved connectivity graph, compatible capacity/state, intake/quality decision, power/backup, catchment or recovery effect.
findings.action: Build authority-approved non-sensitive dike/canal/lock/pump/sewer/intake service zones, separating observed point data from event boundaries and adding intake isolation, sampling, alternate supply and public-health actions.

findings.summary: A2/A27/N-road, bridge, tram and shipping dependencies lack event-valid access semantics.
findings.evidence: The graph has eight logical A2/A27/N210/N408/N409 links and 78 transit stops but no local bridge/lock/canal/tram state, hazard intersection, direction, accessibility, feeder route, hospital/response destination or verified throughput. Prinses Beatrixsluis is the only lock complex on the direct Rotterdam-Amsterdam route, so navigation disruption also has cross-boundary consequences.
findings.action: Add event-valid direction-aware road/tram/bridge/lock/navigation state and destination access using NWB/NDW, operators and RWS notices; static geometry/schedules never imply passage or additive capacity.

findings.summary: St. Antonius emergency-care continuity and access cannot influence first-72-hour decisions.
findings.evidence: RIVM v1.1 reports one 24/7 SEH in GM0356 with eighteen treatment rooms and 22,094 visits in 2025, but no acute obstetrics. The facilities index applies generic service percentages without live occupancy/staffing/diversion, hospital power/water/oxygen/supply dependencies, generator endurance, access, transfer destinations or restoration.
findings.action: Add GHOR/hospital-approved safe aggregate readiness, dependency and transfer states with issue/valid time; retain unavailable sensitive capacity as Unknown and never infer operation from the questionnaire.

findings.summary: Net congestion and first-72-hour preparedness are not converted into evidence-bounded continuity actions.
findings.evidence: The municipality describes both demand/injection congestion, new connection queues and priority categories; the NBNL sample has null withdrawal capacity but exact queues. It also asks households to self-support for 72 hours. No outage/switching state, priority restoration, support-point network, vulnerable-household reach, cash/food/water distribution, communications fallback or verification is modelled.
findings.action: Request Stedin/municipality/VRU-approved aggregate incident and restoration bands plus accountable support/distribution/communication actions; planning queues and public advice never prove live continuity or preparedness.

findings.summary: Local Waterinfo observations and absent local forecast coverage are not reconciled with exact scenario precision.
findings.evidence: Four timestamped observation points are assigned at Doorslag/Lekkanaal, no forecast point is assigned to GM0356, and the national rolling product has zero returned features at some T+48/T+72 horizons. These points correctly do not affect the simulation, yet the model emits exact river severity/depth and recovery without selecting a valid boundary condition.
findings.action: Preserve observation versus forecast classes, point coverage, issue/valid/retrieval time, datum, fault/freshness, horizon and NoData. Bind only a governed station/event adapter; absent forecast coverage must remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Exact T+24-72 flood/service plateaus and rapid direct-hazard clearing contradict explicit recovery uncertainty.
findings.evidence: Most river services are identical from T+24 through T+72 while facilities worsens; compound services likewise plateau; pluvial becomes direct-zero by T+72. The municipal climate vision explicitly says it is unknown when an inundated area becomes dry, passable, habitable or liveable.
findings.action: Replace exact transitions with uncertainty envelopes and accountable milestones for water exclusion, pumping, structural/road/lock inspection, hospital/utilities, intake quality, public health, support, re-entry and consequences beyond T+72.

findings.summary: Coastal, earthquake, wildfire/smoke and cyber results are synthetic exercises rather than all-clear states.
findings.evidence: Coastal direct inundation is zero while wind and incoming coastal evacuation traffic remain relevant; earthquake is direct-zero with residual burden; canonical wildfire has smoke 0.382757 but no local flame; cyber has no selected asset target. No current KNMI/RIVM/RWS/fire/operator event is bound.
findings.action: Keep direct-versus-indirect scope and synthetic labels. Add events only with publisher, version, issue/valid/retrieval time, geometry/target, units, uncertainty, coverage, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: The complete numerical, checkpoint, allocation, ledger and burden-accounting contract passes for GM0356.
findings.evidence: The mandatory gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/deterministic, no-event behavior is exact, municipality/service totals reconcile, ledgers close, burden is monotone, road scope is bounded and layer selection is invariant.
findings.action: Keep GM0356 in regression and add selected-Lek-event, official Fokkesteeg allocation, Waterinfo NoData, hospital continuity, access and Unknown-versus-zero assertions.

corrections.validation: Reconcile HDSR/HWH/RWS/Vitens safe aggregates into current dike, canal/lock, pump/sewer and intake zones with compatible units and effective dates. A point observation is not an inundation surface and empty T+48/T+72 or municipal forecast coverage is NoData, never zero. corrections.validation: Use NWB/NDW, RWS navigation/lock notices, Province/municipality, tram/bus operators, GHOR/RIVM and hospital-approved safe aggregates. residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, navigation notice, hospital status or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality total; null capacity, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.
Generalized municipality/neighbourhood geometry is suitable for display and selection, not dike, breach, hydraulic, rain, sewer, groundwater, terrain, building, asset, intake or route intersection.
The 2018 climate vision is authoritative local mechanism/planning evidence but not a current hydrograph, hydraulic model run, defence state, evacuation plan or present damage estimate.
HDSR's 2024 assessment and Sterke Lekdijk programme prove a strengthening requirement, not live dike strength, breach probability, emergency measure state or completed work.
No selected LIWO/WMCN event footprint, Lek hydrograph, defence/breach state, depth/velocity/arrival/recession series or probability is consumed for GM0356.
Four Doorslag/Lekkanaal Waterinfo records are local point observations, not a flood surface, system threshold, municipal forecast or operational instruction.
No rolling Waterinfo forecast point is assigned inside GM0356 and some national T+48/T+72 horizon responses are empty; this is NoData, never zero water or zero hazard.
No governing local rain hyetograph, climate-atlas/stress-test raster, terrain/intervention edition, groundwater state, sewer-overland model or pump operating state is consumed.
HWH's 146 assigned records have partial contributor coverage and source-specific capacity semantics; registered status/capacity cannot be summed or treated as live without reconciliation.
The Prinses Beatrixsluis and Lekkanaal intake/source-protection programme do not establish current navigation, intake, water quality, contamination, storage, alternate supply or restoration.
NWB/NDW, GTFS and ProRail data do not establish live road/bridge/tram/bus/lock passability, direction, accessibility, emergency throughput or destination access.
RIVM's St. Antonius record does not establish live occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator/oxygen/water endurance, transfer capacity, incident access or restoration.
DUO school and RDI antenna records identify static locations/applications, not people present, shelter/support role, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage or restoration.
One NBNL postcode sample is large-user planning context; its null withdrawal capacity is Unknown and queue/project values are not municipal load, topology, outage, reserve or restoration.
Municipal first-72-hour advice does not prove household preparation, social-network reach, support-point activation, staff, communications, stocks, capacity or endurance.
Registered residents do not equal incident-time people at St. Antonius, schools, offices, shopping centres, business parks, locks, shipping, transit, recreation or events.
The 21.6% age-65 share and other CBS vulnerability proxies do not prove individual assistance need, hospital use or operator restoration priority.
Direct coastal/fire/earthquake zero is a narrow model statement, not absence of incoming evacuation traffic, wind, smoke, seismic, industrial, access, supply or cross-boundary effects.
Recovery after T+72, pre-impact warning, mutual aid, shelter/transfer capacity, hospital/source-water public health and long-term re-entry remain outside locally validated scope.
